title: Defender for Identity retires the classic 'Remote code execution attempt' and pass-the-hash alerts at the end of November 2026
summary: MC1552387 (13 November 2026, act by 30 November): Microsoft Defender for Identity retires two classic alerts in late November 2026 across worldwide, GCC, GCC High and DoD — Remote code execution attempt (external ID 2025) and Suspected identity theft (pass-the-hash, external ID 2036). Microsoft's replacement is an advanced hunting custom detection rule for remote execution (published query on GitHub) and Defender for Endpoint coverage for pass-the-hash on onboarded devices.
why: If your SOC playbooks, SIEM analytics or purple-team scorecards key on these two alert titles or IDs, they will silently stop firing. Pass-the-hash coverage moves to the endpoint, so domain controllers and tier-0 servers that run only the MDI sensor and are not onboarded to MDE become a blind spot.
todo: Find every SIEM rule, automation and runbook that matches the alert titles or external IDs 2025/2036 (Sentinel analytics on SecurityAlert/AlertInfo, SOAR playbooks, ticket mappings).
Create the remote-execution custom detection in Defender XDR advanced hunting from Microsoft's published query, tuned to your admin tooling (recipe on this site).
Confirm that domain controllers, AD CS, AD FS and Entra Connect servers are onboarded to Defender for Endpoint, not only running the MDI sensor.
Re-run your pass-the-hash and remote-execution purple-team test cases after the rollout and record which alert now fires.
